exact_post_wording: Croatia completed 82.5% of the final-third passing in the 2018 World Cup Final. France completed 17.5% — and won 4-2. Field tilt (final-third passing share) isn't the whole story.
metric_definition_and_formula: Field tilt = a team's completed passes starting in the final third (x>80 on StatsBomb's 0-120, attacking-direction-normalised pitch) divided by both teams' combined final-third completed passes.
competition_season_match: FIFA World Cup 2018 Final, Croatia vs France, 2018-07-15, match_id 8658
sample_size: 114 final-third passes out of 650 total completed passes in the match
underlying_row_ids: scratch/wc2018_final_field_tilt_audit.csv (114 rows, StatsBomb event IDs); silver/statsbomb_events/events.parquet WHERE match_id=8658
limitations_caveats: Passing-distribution metric only — does not measure territory, chance quality, or possession value. Reproduced independently via DuckDB SQL (gold/field_tilt_wc2018_final.csv), matches the pandas figure exactly.

competition_season_match: FIFA World Cup 2022 Final, Argentina vs France, 2022-12-18, match_id 3869685
numerator: n/a — direct distance measurement, not a ratio
sample_size: 1 shot event; 8 opposition players captured in its freeze-frame (out of 11 Argentina players on the pitch)
underlying_row_ids: shot event_id 03fb2918-e1e7-4ec8-89ff-7bc5531e853d; scratch/wc2022_final_mbappe_g2_360_audit.csv (12 rows: 1 shooter + 11 freeze-frame entries); silver/statsbomb_360_freeze_frames/frames.parquet WHERE event_uuid = '03fb2918-e1e7-4ec8-89ff-7bc5531e853d'

exact_post_wording: A-League full-back Dylan Pierias covered more sprint distance per 90 this season (326.8m) than Western Sydney's Brandon Borrello (281.4m) — a forward. Running data doesn't care about your position.
metric_definition_and_formula: sprint_distance_p90 = sprint_distance_full_all / minutes_full_all * 90, where minutes_full_all is the player's average minutes per match across the season.
competition_season_match: A-League Men, Australia, 2024/25 season (no single match — season aggregate)
numerator: Pierias: 357.45m total sprint distance per match-average, 98.43 avg minutes/match
denominator: count_match = 22 (Pierias), 24 (Borrello) — matches contributing to the season aggregate
sample_size: 22 matches (Pierias, ~2,165 est. total minutes), 24 matches (Borrello, ~2,226 est. total minutes)
provider_supplied_or_calculated: provider_supplied totals (sprint_distance_full_all, psv99); locally_calculated per-90 rate
limitations_caveats: Full-back vs center-forward — different positions carry different running profiles by role; this is a running-output comparison, not a 'better player' claim.

exact_post_wording: Brisbane Roar's average team width in possession went from 39.2m in the first half to 45.4m in the second (width data only — not a formation claim). Still lost 2-3.
metric_definition_and_formula: avg_width per half = mean of (team_in_possession_width_start + team_in_possession_width_end)/2 across all possession phases in that half, for the team in possession.
competition_season_match: A-League 2024/25, Brisbane Roar FC 2-3 Adelaide United FC, 2024-11-23, match_id 1874553
numerator: sum of per-phase average width across Brisbane's 2nd-half possession phases
denominator: 99 Brisbane possession phases in the 2nd half (89 in the 1st half)
sample_size: 423 possession phases total in the match (188 Brisbane, 235 Adelaide)
provider_supplied_or_calculated: provider_supplied per-phase width fields; locally_calculated half-level average
limitations_caveats: Phase-level snapshots (start/end of each possession phase), not a continuous per-frame trace. Describes measured width only — does not claim a formation change or tactical intent, which would need additional positional evidence. Gold (DuckDB SQL) figures differ by <0.3m from an earlier pandas prototype due to null-row averaging handling; the SQL figures here are the ones of record.
